title: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord
body:
Read the chapter → [1 Samuel 12](/bible/1-samuel/12)

## Introduction

This session covers [1 Samuel 12](/bible/1-samuel/12) through 15, heavy chapters in the rise and fall of king Saul. In chapter 12 Samuel gives his farewell address: he establishes his own blamelessness, rehearses the righteous acts of the Most High from Egypt through the judges, rebukes Israel for demanding a king when the Lord was their king, and calls down thunder and rain in wheat harvest to prove the wickedness of that request. In chapter 13 Saul begins to show he is not fit to be king, making haste in time of trouble by offering the burnt offering instead of waiting for Samuel. In chapter 14 Jonathan and his armor bearer take on the Philistine garrison alone, showing there is no restraint to the Lord to save by many or by few. In chapter 15 the Lord commands Saul to utterly destroy Amalek; Saul obeys partially, and partial obedience is counted as rebellion: to obey is better than sacrifice, and rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft.

**[1 Samuel 12:1](/bible/1-samuel/12#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/1-samuel/12#v1)</sup> And Samuel said unto all Israel, Behold, I have hearkened unto your voice in all that ye said unto me, and have made a king over you.

- At the end of chapter 11 Israel crowned Saul at Gilgal. Back in chapter 8 the people had pressured Samuel because they wanted to be like the nations round about them, and the Most High led him to choose Saul the son of Kish.
- This is the aftermath speech. Samuel is putting it on record: I hearkened unto your voice in all that ye said unto me and made a king over you; whatever happens from here came from what you asked for.

**[1 Samuel 12:2-5](/bible/1-samuel/12#v2)**

> <sup>[2](/bible/1-samuel/12#v2)</sup> And now, behold, the king walketh before you: and I am old and grayheaded; and, behold, my sons are with you: and I have walked before you from my childhood unto this day.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/1-samuel/12#v3)</sup> Behold, here I am: witness against me before the Lord, and before his anointed: whose ox have I taken? or whose ass have I taken? or whom have I defrauded? whom have I oppressed? or of whose hand have I received any bribe to blind mine eyes therewith? and I will restore it you.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/1-samuel/12#v4)</sup> And they said, Thou hast not defrauded us, nor oppressed us, neither hast thou taken ought of any man’s hand.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/1-samuel/12#v5)</sup> And he said unto them, The Lord is witness against you, and his anointed is witness this day, that ye have not found ought in my hand. And they answered, He is witness.

- Samuel establishes his blamelessness before he reasons with them. He walked before Israel from his childhood unto this day; whose ox or ass has he taken, whom has he defrauded or oppressed, from whose hand has he taken any bribe? Speak up now and he will restore it.
- The people answer that he has not defrauded nor oppressed them nor taken anything from any man's hand, and the Lord and his anointed are witness that day. Samuel was never a bad guy to the nation of Israel, and the whole congregation confirms it.

**[1 Samuel 12:6-7](/bible/1-samuel/12#v6)**

> <sup>[6](/bible/1-samuel/12#v6)</sup> And Samuel said unto the people, It is the Lord that advanced Moses and Aaron, and that brought your fathers up out of the land of Egypt.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/1-samuel/12#v7)</sup> Now therefore stand still, that I may reason with you before the Lord of all the righteous acts of the Lord, which he did to you and to your fathers.

- It is the Lord that advanced Moses and Aaron and brought your fathers up out of the land of Egypt. Now stand still, that Samuel may reason with them before the Lord of all the righteous acts of the Lord which he did to them and to their fathers.

  Precepts:
  - **[Psalms 103:7](/bible/psalms/103#v7)**
    > <sup>[7](/bible/psalms/103#v7)</sup> He made known his ways unto Moses, his acts unto the children of Israel.

    He made known his ways unto Moses, his acts unto the children of Israel; the righteous acts Samuel rehearses are those acts.

**[1 Samuel 12:8-11](/bible/1-samuel/12#v8)**

> <sup>[8](/bible/1-samuel/12#v8)</sup> When Jacob was come into Egypt, and your fathers cried unto the Lord, then the Lord sent Moses and Aaron, which brought forth your fathers out of Egypt, and made them dwell in this place.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/1-samuel/12#v9)</sup> And when they forgat the Lord their God, he sold them into the hand of Sisera, captain of the host of Hazor, and into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the king of Moab, and they fought against them.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/1-samuel/12#v10)</sup> And they cried unto the Lord, and said, We have sinned, because we have forsaken the Lord, and have served Baalim and Ashtaroth: but now deliver us out of the hand of our enemies, and we will serve thee.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/1-samuel/12#v11)</sup> And the Lord sent Jerubbaal, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivered you out of the hand of your enemies on every side, and ye dwelled safe.

- When Jacob was come into Egypt and your fathers cried unto the Lord, the Lord sent Moses and Aaron and made Israel dwell in this place. When they forgat the Lord he sold them into the hand of Sisera, captain of the host of Hazor, and of the Philistines, and of the king of Moab; this is the history of the book of Judges, starting in chapter 4.
- They cried unto the Lord and confessed they had sinned in forsaking him and serving Baalim and Ashtaroth. That is the same lesson Samuel taught in chapter 7: when the Philistines beat Israel, they went and got the ark of the covenant, got beat even worse, and lost the ark. It is not just about having the ark of the covenant among you; you have to put away the idols and stop serving Baalim and Ashtaroth.
- So the Lord sent Jerubbaal, which is Gideon, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivered Israel out of the hand of their enemies on every side, and they dwelled safe. None of those saviors had to wear a crown.

  Precepts:
  - **[Judges 8:22](/bible/judges/8#v22)**
    > <sup>[22](/bible/judges/8#v22)</sup> Then the men of Israel said unto Gideon, Rule thou over us, both thou, and thy son, and thy son’s son also: for thou hast delivered us from the hand of Midian.

    After Gideon led the three hundred, the men of Israel said, Rule thou over us, both thou and thy son and thy son's son also, for thou hast delivered us from the hand of Midian.
  - **[Judges 8:23](/bible/judges/8#v23)**
    > <sup>[23](/bible/judges/8#v23)</sup> And Gideon said unto them, I will not rule over you, neither shall my son rule over you: the Lord shall rule over you.

    Gideon refused: I will not rule over you, neither shall my son rule over you; the Lord shall rule over you. He knew that if thrones were set up, the people would put their trust and faith in the king instead of the Most High; it was never the Lord's intention to set kings in the flesh over Israel, he was to be our king.

**[1 Samuel 12:12-15](/bible/1-samuel/12#v12)**

> <sup>[12](/bible/1-samuel/12#v12)</sup> And when ye saw that Nahash the king of the children of Ammon came against you, ye said unto me, Nay; but a king shall reign over us: when the Lord your God was your king.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/1-samuel/12#v13)</sup> Now therefore behold the king whom ye have chosen, and whom ye have desired! and, behold, the Lord hath set a king over you.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/1-samuel/12#v14)</sup> If ye will fear the Lord, and serve him, and obey his voice, and not rebel against the commandment of the Lord, then shall both ye and also the king that reigneth over you continue following the Lord your God:
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/1-samuel/12#v15)</sup> But if ye will not obey the voice of the Lord, but rebel against the commandment of the Lord, then shall the hand of the Lord be against you, as it was against your fathers.

- When Nahash king of the children of Ammon came against them, Israel said, Nay, but a king shall reign over us, when the Lord their God was their king. That demand exposed their disbelief in the Lord; they wanted a king they could see and touch, because all the nations around them had kings.
- Now behold the king whom ye have chosen and whom ye have desired. If ye will fear the Lord and serve him and obey his voice and not rebel against the commandment of the Lord, then shall both ye and also the king that reigneth over you continue following the Lord your God. If you and your king do not rebel against the voice of the Lord, the ultimate king, you will be all right.
- Moses, in the spirit of the Lord, knew exactly what Israel would do once they came into the land, and wrote the law of the king ahead of time.

  Precepts:
  - **[Deuteronomy 17:14](/bible/deuteronomy/17#v14)**
    > <sup>[14](/bible/deuteronomy/17#v14)</sup> When thou art come unto the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee, and shalt possess it, and shalt dwell therein, and shalt say, I will set a king over me, like as all the nations that are about me;

    Moses prophesied Israel would come into the land and say, I will set a king over me, like as all the nations that are about me.
  - **[Deuteronomy 17:15](/bible/deuteronomy/17#v15)**
    > <sup>[15](/bible/deuteronomy/17#v15)</sup> Thou shalt in any wise set him king over thee, whom the Lord thy God shall choose: one from among thy brethren shalt thou set king over thee: thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother.

    The king must be one whom the Lord thy God shall choose, one from among thy brethren; thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother.
  - **[Deuteronomy 17:20](/bible/deuteronomy/17#v20)**
    > <sup>[20](/bible/deuteronomy/17#v20)</sup> That his heart be not lifted up above his brethren, and that he turn not aside from the commandment, to the right hand, or to the left: to the end that he may prolong his days in his kingdom, he, and his children, in the midst of Israel.

    His heart must not be lifted up above his brethren, and he must not turn aside from the commandment to the right hand or to the left, to the end that he may prolong his days in his kingdom, he and his children in the midst of Israel; that is exactly what Samuel just told the people.

- But if ye will not obey the voice of the Lord, but rebel against the commandment of the Lord, then shall the hand of the Lord be against you, as it was against your fathers. Samuel repeats it because Israelites require repetition.

  Precepts:
  - **[Deuteronomy 28:15](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v15)**
    > <sup>[15](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v15)</sup> But it shall come to pass, if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee:

    If thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes, all these curses shall come upon thee and overtake thee.
  - **[Deuteronomy 28:36](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v36)**
    > <sup>[36](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v36)</sup> The Lord shall bring thee, and thy king which thou shalt set over thee, unto a nation which neither thou nor thy fathers have known; and there shalt thou serve other gods, wood and stone.

    The Lord shall bring thee, and thy king which thou shalt set over thee, unto a nation which neither thou nor thy fathers have known; if you and your king disobey, the Lord sends you and your king into subjection to the other nations.

**[1 Samuel 12:16-18](/bible/1-samuel/12#v16)**

> <sup>[16](/bible/1-samuel/12#v16)</sup> Now therefore stand and see this great thing, which the Lord will do before your eyes.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/1-samuel/12#v17)</sup> Is it not wheat harvest to day? I will call unto the Lord, and he shall send thunder and rain; that ye may perceive and see that your wickedness is great, which ye have done in the sight of the Lord, in asking you a king.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/1-samuel/12#v18)</sup> So Samuel called unto the Lord; and the Lord sent thunder and rain that day: and all the people greatly feared the Lord and Samuel.

- Is it not wheat harvest today? To demonstrate how wicked Israel was for asking a king, Samuel calls unto the Lord for thunder and rain on the very day they expected clear skies to gather the wheat. The Lord sent thunder and rain that day, and all the people greatly feared the Lord and Samuel.

  Precepts:
  - **[2 Samuel 22:14](/bible/2-samuel/22#v14)**
    > <sup>[14](/bible/2-samuel/22#v14)</sup> The Lord thundered from heaven, and the most High uttered his voice.

    The Lord thundered from heaven, and the most High uttered his voice; imagine how terrified they were when that voice went off.
  - **[2 Samuel 22:15](/bible/2-samuel/22#v15)**
    > <sup>[15](/bible/2-samuel/22#v15)</sup> And he sent out arrows, and scattered them; lightning, and discomfited them.

    And he sent out arrows, and scattered them; lightning, and discomfited them; that is the power the Most High put on display.

**[1 Samuel 12:19](/bible/1-samuel/12#v19)**

> <sup>[19](/bible/1-samuel/12#v19)</sup> And all the people said unto Samuel, Pray for thy servants unto the Lord thy God, that we die not: for we have added unto all our sins this evil, to ask us a king.

- Once the Lord thundered, the people acknowledged their folly: pray for thy servants unto the Lord thy God, that we die not, for we have added unto all our sins this evil, to ask us a king. Now they confess they were dead wrong for asking for a king.

**[1 Samuel 12:20](/bible/1-samuel/12#v20)**

> <sup>[20](/bible/1-samuel/12#v20)</sup> And Samuel said unto the people, Fear not: ye have done all this wickedness: yet turn not aside from following the Lord, but serve the Lord with all your heart;

- Fear not: ye have done all this wickedness, yet turn not aside from following the Lord, but serve the Lord with all your heart. Yes, you did all this wickedness, but now you get it; after all the wickedness you have done, still serve the Lord. That is heavy.

  Precepts:
  - **[Proverbs 24:16](/bible/proverbs/24#v16)**
    > <sup>[16](/bible/proverbs/24#v16)</sup> For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.

    This is really a precept for the just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again; the fall does not end your service to the Most High.

**[1 Samuel 12:21](/bible/1-samuel/12#v21)**

> <sup>[21](/bible/1-samuel/12#v21)</sup> And turn ye not aside: for then should ye go after vain things, which cannot profit nor deliver; for they are vain.

- Turn ye not aside, for then should ye go after vain things which cannot profit nor deliver, for they are vain. Something you make with your own hands is not going to make thunder and rain come on your harvest day to show you how wicked you are; idols cannot help you or save you.
- Our people do the same thing today, icing out crosses and things of that nature that cannot do a thing for them; those are the vain things our people follow after. Samuel warned Israel not to do it, and over a span of time that is exactly what they ended up doing.

  Precepts:
  - **[Jeremiah 2:5](/bible/jeremiah/2#v5)**
    > <sup>[5](/bible/jeremiah/2#v5)</sup> Thus saith the Lord, What iniquity have your fathers found in me, that they are gone far from me, and have walked after vanity, and are become vain?

    What iniquity have your fathers found in me, that they are gone far from me, and have walked after vanity, and are become vain?

**[1 Samuel 12:22](/bible/1-samuel/12#v22)**

> <sup>[22](/bible/1-samuel/12#v22)</sup> For the Lord will not forsake his people for his great name’s sake: because it hath pleased the Lord to make you his people.

- The Lord will not forsake his people for his great name's sake, because it hath pleased the Lord to make you his people. That is part of the comfort of the scriptures: he may purge his people, but he will never exterminate the Israelites, for his name's sake.
- Test that against the doctrine that says the Most High cast off Israel after Christ. Paul, whose writings that doctrine misinterprets, said the same thing Samuel said.

  Precepts:
  - **[Romans 11:1](/bible/romans/11#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/romans/11#v1)</sup> I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.

    Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.
  - **[Romans 11:2](/bible/romans/11#v2)**
    > <sup>[2](/bible/romans/11#v2)</sup> God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew. Wot ye not what the scripture saith of Elias? how he maketh intercession to God against Israel, saying,

    God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew; the Lord has not cast off Israel.

**[1 Samuel 12:23](/bible/1-samuel/12#v23)**

> <sup>[23](/bible/1-samuel/12#v23)</sup> Moreover as for me, God forbid that I should sin against the Lord in ceasing to pray for you: but I will teach you the good and the right way:

- Marinate on this verse. God forbid that I should sin against the Lord in ceasing to pray for you; but I will teach you the good and the right way. Samuel says that as a leader who loved his nation, if he stopped praying for them, that itself would put him in sin.
- For those who battle with prayer, meditate on that: ceasing to pray for your nation puts you in sin.

  Precepts:
  - **[Job 15:4](/bible/job/15#v4)**
    > <sup>[4](/bible/job/15#v4)</sup> Yea, thou castest off fear, and restrainest prayer before God.

    Yea, thou castest off fear, and restrainest prayer before God; restraining prayer shows you are starting to lack fear of the Most High. If you want him in your life, you cannot restrain prayer from him, any more than you would let communication die with someone you wanted to keep.

**[1 Samuel 12:24-25](/bible/1-samuel/12#v24)**

> <sup>[24](/bible/1-samuel/12#v24)</sup> Only fear the Lord, and serve him in truth with all your heart: for consider how great things he hath done for you.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/1-samuel/12#v25)</sup> But if ye shall still do wickedly, ye shall be consumed, both ye and your king.

- Only fear the Lord and serve him in truth with all your heart, and consider how great things he hath done for you. But if ye shall still do wickedly, after the speech, the warning, and the thunder, ye shall be consumed, both ye and your king.
- That is what [Deuteronomy 28:36](/bible/deuteronomy/28#v36) said: you and the king you set over you will be brought into subjection to the other nations. Samuel's exhortation was to get their minds on the right track: you asked for the wrong thing, but now that you have it, keep the commandments and you will be all right.
